<description>
This picks up #24963.

`walletprocesspsbt` takes four settings after the PSBT, three of them booleans, so a positional call reads `walletprocesspsbt "psbt" true "ALL" true false`, and each new setting becomes one more positional parameter (#32857 would add a sixth). This moves the four settings into an options object as the second parameter. Calls that work today, by position or by name, keep working.

For the old positional form, the second position accepts either the options object or the old `sign` boolean, which needs a parameter to declare one type per alias. The other three settings stay as hidden positional parameters. A parameter passed by name must have the type declared for that name, so `options=true` is rejected instead of being read as `sign=true`.

Changes compared to #24963, besides the rebase on the current RPC framework.

- `getopenrpcinfo` describes the second parameter as an object or a boolean.
- A call mixing positional and named arguments, such as `walletprocesspsbt <psbt> true finalize=false` with `-named`, works as on master instead of failing with "specified twice".
- The type check by name no longer reads the wrong name after an options object built from named options, which made `walletcreatefundedpsbt outputs=... add_inputs=true bip32derivs=false` fail with "JSON value of type object is not of expected type object".
- A null option means the default, as a null named argument does on master.
- From review on #24963, the options are checked before the wallet sync and the PSBT decode, and a test mixes positional and named arguments.
- Unit tests for the framework changes.

`descriptorprocesspsbt` and `createwallet` I will do as follow-ups if this is accepted first.
</description>

<commits>
2499edf391 rpc: Support different types for param aliases

An RPC parameter can have aliases but only one type. Let it declare a
type per alias, so that one position can take a new options object
under one name and the old boolean under another. Replacing positional
parameters with an options object without breaking existing callers
needs this.

MatchesType accepts any of the declared types, and GetArgMap lists each
alias with its own type, so the client conversion table is checked per
name.

Co-authored-by: jeanpablojp <me@jeanpablo.jp>

60cf5faf1a rpc: Describe all types of a param in OpenRPC

getopenrpcinfo builds the schema of a parameter from its first type
only, so a parameter that takes an options object or a boolean would be
described as an object. Describe it with a oneOf holding one schema per
declared type.

c3db835afd rpc: Keep mixed positional and named calls working

A named-only option that a positional parameter also accepts by name
(also_positional) always goes into the options object. When positional
arguments passed in "args" already take the position of that object,
the call fails with "specified twice", although the option could go to
the positional parameter of the same name. Pass it there instead.

No RPC has this layout yet. The next commit gives walletprocesspsbt
one, and without this change a call such as
`walletprocesspsbt <psbt> true finalize=false` with -named, which works
today, would start to fail.

d24c8ea83d rpc, wallet: Convert walletprocesspsbt to options

Move sign, sighashtype, bip32derivs and finalize into an options object
as the second parameter, so that new settings do not have to become
more positional parameters.

Existing calls keep working. The second position still accepts the sign
boolean, sighashtype, bip32derivs and finalize stay as hidden positional
parameters, and all four can still be passed by name. A null option
means the default, as a null named argument did before.

The options are read before waiting for the wallet to sync and decoding
the PSBT, so invalid options are reported first. The conversion check
in rpc_help.py compares sets now, because sign is listed at position 1
both as an option and as an alias.

Co-authored-by: jeanpablojp <me@jeanpablo.jp>

54023e9325 rpc: Enforce the declared type of named params

A parameter passed by name must have the type declared for that name,
so walletprocesspsbt rejects options=true instead of reading it as
sign=true. A parameter passed by position can still have any of its
declared types.

transformNamedArguments records the name each parameter was passed
under. Holes and an options object built from named options get no
name, so the parameters after them keep their own.

Co-authored-by: jeanpablojp <me@jeanpablo.jp>

348688bb8f test: Check walletprocesspsbt option errors

Cover options passed by name with the wrong type, an options field with
the wrong type, an unknown option, and an options object followed by
more positional parameters.

Co-authored-by: jeanpablojp <me@jeanpablo.jp>
</commits>
